Owner-hours: FULL-TIME hands-on, 40-50 hr/wk (sales, quoting, production supervision, hiring, AR/AP); routes/pure distribution can be leaner (~20-30 hr) but have a lower ceiling. Not passive.
result.category_verdict: A solid, cheap-multiple, recession-resilient "boring cash flow" vein — but a MODERATE, not top-tier, fit for this founder. Economics are genuinely good (2.0-2.75x SDE, 30-40% owner-operator yield, seller financing common). Best sub-play: niche manufacturing + custom fabrication (esp. the Buncombe NC signage-materials/CNC/plastics shop, #1) — it fits all-cash, has diversified revenue, and overlaps Hooman's CutLog/CNC domain. Print/promo (Minuteman) offers the highest SDE at the lowest multiple but rides a declining print substrate. AVOID the 4-5x distribution and delivery-route listings (overpriced, thin margins, no AI edge). Core caveat: these are full-time hands-on US operator JOBS where his AI/data skill is only a margin-improver, not a core fit. Recommend as a value/cash-flow backstop, and run a PARALLEL CANADIAN search to unlock BDC leverage and sidestep the E-2 visa + no-SBA constraints.
result.financing_notes: SBA 7(a)/504 is effectively OFF THE TABLE for Hooman (requires US citizen/LPR) — yet several listings (metal distribution, many sign franchises) are SBA-marketed, so their prices assume a leveraged US buyer he can't be. His real universe is ALL-CASH <=$500K or all-cash + SELLER NOTE. Seller financing IS available on the two best deals (Sign NM #1, Minuteman Print #2): a 60-70% cash down + 30-40% seller note (3-5 yr, 6-8%) lets the $600K Minuteman fit inside $500K cash. Franchised listings require franchisor approval of a non-resident buyer — an added hurdle. THE REAL GATE IS IMMIGRATION, not the loan: to operate a US business on the ground Hooman likely needs an E-2 treaty-investor visa (Canada IS an E-2 treaty country and ~$500K clears the 'substantial investment' bar — a genuine path, but the #1 diligence item). Canadian alternative: BDC/bank acquisition financing exists for Canada-domiciled sign shops/distributors, which would unlock leverage AND avoid the visa problem — worth a parallel ON/BC search.
result.hooman_fit: Edge that helps: these firms run on spreadsheets, paper quotes, and tribal knowledge — an AI/data-engineering owner can build quoting automation, CRM + reorder/route optimization, inventory demand forecasting, and marketing automation the retiring owners never touched (plausible 10-20% margin lift). The Buncombe NC CNC/wide-format/plastics-cutting fabricator directly overlaps his CutLog/laser-cutting domain. Where his edge is IRRELEVANT: the day-to-day job is local B2B sales, walk-in service, labor management, and physical production — not his strength or interest. His analytical/diligence ability is worth more in picking a cheap, clean deal than in running it. Net founder-market fit: MODERATE — he'd be buying a hands-on trade-services job with a software-improvement upside, not a software company.

result.category_economics: This category prices on SDE/net-profit multiples, NOT revenue. Empire Flippers quotes multiples in MONTHS of net profit; live listings on 2026-07-03 ran 26x-37x monthly = ~2.2x-3.1x annual SDE. BizBuySell's asking/cash-flow implied ~1.5x-4.5x SDE. Typical clean buy is ~2.0-3.0x SDE. A ~$500K all-cash purchase at ~2.5x buys roughly $165K-$250K annual SDE = ~$14K-$21K/mo pre-tax owner cash flow. Paper cash yield is very high (33-50%), but that discount is the market pricing in real decay risk. Owner-hours: 20-40+/wk for a genuine single-brand FBA business (inventory, PPC, suppliers, reviews); full-time for multi-store ops. "Turnkey/automated" hour claims are marketing.
result.category_verdict: Weak-to-moderate vein for the BEST ~$500K buy. Highest headline yield and easiest all-cash fit of any category, but the WORST durability: single-brand Amazon FBA is a platform-dependent single-point-of-failure (account suspension, review purge, PPC/fee inflation, Chinese copycats, Amazon policy changes). The low 2-3x multiples are earned, not a bargain. Best sub-play: an aged (5+yr), multi-channel brand with real off-Amazon revenue (own Shopify + TikTok Shop), diversified SKUs, defensible brand/IP, bought all-cash at <=2.5x SDE with a LARGE seller note/earnout to offload decay risk onto the seller. On a risk-adjusted basis this should rank below cash-flowing service/'boring' businesses.
result.financing_notes: SBA 7(a) (10% down, 90% financed) is the entire leverage engine of the US FBA-acquisition market, and Hooman as a CANADIAN citizen almost certainly cannot use it. This removes the standard playbook but is actually an ADVANTAGE for an all-cash buyer: SBA-dependent bidders get frozen out of sub-$700K deals when credit tightens, and sellers prize a fast all-cash close. He can comfortably buy any listing here within $500K all-cash. Seller notes/earnouts are standard AND strongly advisable in this category — structure 30-50% as a seller note tied to trailing revenue to shift decay risk to the seller (the single biggest lever). Canadian banks/BDC will generally NOT lend against a US Amazon FBA account (intangible, foreign-platform collateral), so treat this as all-cash + seller-note only. Buying on Amazon US needs a US entity/EIN and sales-tax handling (~$5-15K setup + accounting).
result.hooman_fit: Strong on the improvement levers: PPC/ad optimization, keyword/listing data analysis, demand forecasting, inventory/reorder automation, and internal tooling are exactly what separates a well-run FBA brand from a decaying one — his data/AI/EE background is genuine value-creation, not decoration. BUT his edge is irrelevant to the actual moat, which is brand, reviews, supplier relationships, and Amazon goodwill — no ML fixes a suspended Seller Central account. Owner-dependence sits in supplier relationships and account health, both of which transfer with real handover risk. Full-time hands-on ownership is realistic and in-scope for him.

result.category_verdict: STRONG vein — arguably the single best category for Hooman specifically, because it maximizes his two edges (technical/code diligence + AI/infra value creation) and delivers the best cash-on-cash yield per dollar (~33% at a fair 3x SDE all-cash). It also fits the all-cash-only Canadian reality: real durable sub-$500K vertical B2B SaaS trades at ~3x SDE and is buyable outright with cash to spare. Best sub-play: boring, bootstrapped, regulation-adjacent VERTICAL B2B SaaS at ~3x SDE (EH&S/SDS compliance software; long-lived email-service-provider SaaS) — sticky recurring revenue, mandate-driven demand, diversified customers, fairly priced, improvable by an AI/infra engineer. Avoid within the category: consumer AI-wrapper apps (commoditizable by model providers), "SaaS" that is really an SEO/service agency (owner-labor-dependent, no tech edge), declining-revenue assets sold at a fake "discount", and ARR-priced growth stories at 15–20x SDE.
result.financing_notes: SBA 7(a)/504 is realistically OFF THE TABLE. SBA SOP 50 10 requires the operating business to be ≥51% owned by US citizens or lawful permanent residents; a Canadian citizen with no US green card generally cannot use standard SBA leverage. Since nearly all listings here are US-based, most US bank acquisition financing is also unavailable to him — verify his exact residency status before assuming any US-loan path. Canadian options (BDC, Canadian banks) finance acquisitions but strongly prefer a Canadian-domiciled target with Canadian cash flow, so they are a poor fit for buying a US software company. Practical reality: treat every deal as ALL-CASH within ~$500K, with a SELLER NOTE / vendor take-back (10–30%, paid from the business's own cash flow) as the only realistic leverage — a seller note requires no citizenship and aligns seller incentives. The strongest in-band picks (EH&S SDS $325K, email SaaS $345K, EF #94153 $377K) fit all-cash with buffer; the $500K healthcare deals fit all-cash with no buffer.
result.hooman_fit: Best-mapped category to his skills. His edge is IRRELEVANT/a trap on: the SEO/agency "recurring revenue" listings that dominate this band (really full-time service shops), and consumer AI-wrapper apps (thin moat — his own knowledge says model providers eat the feature). A ~$500K all-cash buy at ~2.3x SDE implies ~$180–220K annual SDE = ~$15–18.3K/mo owner cash and a ~35–45% pre-tax cash yield on equity; if you hire a GM to replace the owner, net drops to roughly $110–150K/yr (~$9–12.5K/mo) and ~25–30% yield. result.category_verdict: Strong vein — arguably the best 'boring cash flow' category at $500K: cheap 2.1–2.8x SDE multiples, 30–45% cash yields, durable AI-safe demand, deep supply. Two Hooman-specific gates decide it: (1) avoid license-gated trades (his EE degree does NOT grant an HVAC/plumbing/electrical contractor license) and pick a no-license route model; (2) SBA leverage is off the table for him, so plan all-cash or a seller note. Best sub-play: a RECURRING ROUTE business — residential pest control (lowest recurring multiple at 2.10x, applicator license is exam-attainable) or pool-service route — with 150+ recurring accounts, ~$180–220K SDE, ~2.0–2.5x, seller carrying 40–50%. Concrete targets: OKC pest ($650K/$317K SDE, needs note), Camden NJ pest ($500K/$180K, 1000+ contracts, all-cash), Exton PA bed-bug ($450K/$192K), and the pool routes ($257–275K, all-cash). result.financing_notes: As a Canadian citizen / non-US person, Hooman almost certainly CANNOT use SBA 7(a)/504 — SBA requires ≥20% owners to be US citizens or green-card holders; a work-visa holder (TN/H-1B via Adobe) generally does not qualify. This removes the standard US '10% down + SBA covers 90%' leverage that most of these US asking prices implicitly assume, so FLAG it on every US deal. Practically he is an all-cash buyer: with $500K he cleanly covers the ~$150–220K SDE tier (2–2.5x) outright, and cash offers can win on speed/price. To reach the $500–700K tier (e.g. the OKC $317K-SDE pest deal, Moore OK lawn, FL HVAC) he needs SELLER FINANCING / vendor take-back — common in this category and offered on several listings (bed-bug deal advertises bank financing; Mosquito Shield offers owner financing). Target 50–60% cash down + 40–50% seller note over ~5 yrs; the SDE easily services it. If instead he buys a business IN CANADA, financing is materially easier: BDC and the Canada Small Business Financing Program (CSBFP) plus major-bank acquisition lending are open to citizens. ACTION: verify his exact US visa/residency status before assuming any US-loan path; if buying US, plan around all-cash + seller note.
result.hooman_fit: Good fit IF he targets route/recurring, no-license models (pool, lawn, pest, window/commercial cleaning). His AI/ML + data-engineering edge is a real margin lever there: most incumbents run on paper/spreadsheets, so route-density optimization, automated dispatch/scheduling, dynamic pricing, churn/renewal prediction, and review-generation automation create genuine value — plus his diligence/analytical ability lets him find mispriced deals (the ~1x-SDE wildlife listings and ~1.2x FL-HVAC outlier are either bargains or hiding something and warrant hard diligence). Where his edge is IRRELEVANT: local labor management (hiring/retaining/replacing techs, no-shows, turnover) is the real daily grind and is not a software problem; and trade licensing (HVAC/plumbing/electrical) is a hard blocker his EE degree doesn't solve — he'd need to retain the seller as qualifying party or hire a license-holder. result.category_economics: Small franchise resales trade ~2.0-3.0x SDE (Duck Donuts ~2.7x on $187K SDE; Koala ~1.9x; Budget Blinds ~2.7x). They're cheaper than comparable independents due to royalty drag (typ. 5-8% of revenue), transfer fees, and franchisor buyer-approval. BizBuySell Q1-2026 median small-biz sale = $350K on $165,256 median cash flow (~2.1x); franchise resales cluster here. Unlevered all-cash yield looks like ~35-40% of price, BUT the quoted cash flow is SDE (includes owner's full-time labor). Subtract a ~$70-90K manager salary to run it hands-off and the true passive yield falls sharply. Owner-hours: sub-$500K units are overwhelmingly owner-OPERATED, not semi-absentee. A ~$500K budget buys EITHER one owner-operated unit at full SDE OR a small multi-unit with a GM but thinner net owner cash flow. Duck Donuts (3 units, 25-50 staff, store managers) is the rare listing that's genuinely close to manager-run at this price.
result.category_verdict: MEDIUM vein — real cash flow exists but structurally poor fit for THIS buyer. Three stacked headwinds: (1) No SBA means he pays full ~$500K ALL-CASH while the market is priced for leveraged US buyers putting 10% down — franchise units are the canonical SBA-financed asset class, so this is the category most penalized by his citizenship. (2) Royalty drag + franchisor control over product/pricing/tech deliberately remove the levers where his AI/data/software edge creates value — he'd be an operator, not a builder. (3) 'Semi-absentee' is largely a myth sub-$500K; most units need a hands-on owner. Best sub-play: a HOME-SERVICES resale with recurring revenue + route density + team in place (Budget Blinds $425K/~$159K SDE all-cash; Pool Maintenance $240K cheapest recurring entry), where analytics/marketing automation genuinely lifts a sleepy unit. Duck Donuts is the best true multi-unit but food/labor-heavy. AVOID boutique fitness (chronic low cash flow, high resale churn). Not a lead vein — treat as fallback.
result.financing_notes: SBA 7(a)/504 is OFF the table for Hooman (requires US citizen or lawful permanent resident). The classic '10% down (~$50K) + SBA covers the rest' playbook that US buyers use for exactly these franchise resales does NOT apply — he faces the FULL ~$500K as all-cash. This is the single biggest structural disadvantage in this category. Workable paths: (a) ALL-CASH within $500K — Duck Donuts ($500K), Budget Blinds ($425K), Home Inspection ($399K), Pool Maintenance ($240K) fit; Koala ($649K) and Houston Auto ($550K) do NOT. (b) SELLER NOTE / vendor take-back — common on franchise resales (10-30%, 3-5yr), realistic way to stretch to $600-700K or preserve cash; franchisor still must approve the buyer. (c) Canadian BDC/bank — finance business acquisitions but strongly prefer the target be IN CANADA / a Canadian entity; a US-located franchise unit is hard to finance from Canada. FLAG: operating a US franchise hands-on as a Canadian likely needs an E-2 treaty-investor visa; passive/remote ownership needs a genuine US manager. Cleanest fit = a CANADIAN franchise resale (BDC + seller VTB, no visa/tax friction) — but the deals captured here are US listings, so a dedicated Canadian scan (Sunbelt Canada, businessesforsale.com/canada, CFA member resales) is warranted before committing.
result.hooman_fit: Edge helps most in home services with route density, scheduling, and CRM (Pool Maintenance, Budget Blinds, Koala, mobile floor covering) — his analytics + marketing-automation can lift a sleepy unit's lead-gen and utilization, and physical presence is optional. His diligence alpha (reading an FDD, cohort-analyzing recurring revenue, correctly pricing royalty drag) is a real advantage in buying well. Edge is largely IRRELEVANT in food (Duck Donuts), fitness, senior care, education franchises — the franchisor controls product/pricing/brand/tech and deliberately removes the software-and-data levers where he creates value; he'd be an operator, not a builder, and his AI/ML skillset is mostly wasted. Time: to keep the Adobe job he needs a genuinely manager-run multi-unit (rare and pricier at this budget); otherwise these are hands-on, full-time owner-operator businesses.

result.category_verdict: Yes for LAUNDROMATS specifically; mixed-to-weak for the rest. Laundromats are the strongest ~$500K vein: uniquely they are simultaneously cash-fit for a non-SBA Canadian buyer, high-yield (real ~3x SDE deals throw off 15-25%), semi-absentee, AI-/recession-safe, and directly diligenceable with Hooman's data skills (regress water/sewer/electric utility bills against reported revenue to catch inflated 'cash flow'). Best sub-play = a laundromat bought all-cash or with a seller note, chosen on VERIFIED utility data + a 10+ year secure lease + recent equipment. Self-storage is the better long-term asset (appreciating, most passive, pricing power) but the worst fit at $500K without SBA leverage — quality facilities are real-estate-priced at 5-7% caps and $1M+, so all-cash yield is only ~6%; it would only work as a small Canadian facility with BDC/bank debt. Car washes (self-serve) are cash-fit and high-yield but the most operationally fragile (maintenance, weather, a new tunnel next door). Vending/ATM is cheapest and easiest to enter but the weakest moat/durability. Net: pursue laundromats hard, cherry-pick one self-serve car wash with real estate, treat storage as a Canadian-only or note-only play, and use vending only as a low-stakes 'learn ops' entry.
result.financing_notes: CRITICAL: SBA 7(a)/504 is OFF the table for Hooman. As of March 2025 (Executive Order 14159) the SBA banned non-citizens/non-permanent-residents from SBA-guaranteed loans; the prior rule that let foreign nationals own <=49% and still qualify was eliminated. A Canadian citizen with no US green card CANNOT use the standard '10% down + SBA' leverage that most US laundromat/car-wash/storage buyers rely on. Consequences and alternatives: (1) Model every US deal as ALL-CASH <=$500K, or (2) SELLER FINANCING / VENDOR TAKE-BACK — common in this category, sellers routinely carry 20-50% over 3-7 years; this is Hooman's single most important lever and lets a ~$700-900K asset fit inside ~$400-500K cash down (e.g., Houston Super-Sized laundromat, Cedar Rapids car wash+RE, Tampa vending route). (3) CANADIAN financing (BDC / Canadian banks) really only helps if he buys a CANADIAN laundromat/storage/car wash — BDC and Canadian banks do not conveniently mortgage a US hard asset for him. (4) Conventional US commercial bank / credit union is possible but wants a US entity, US credit history, 25-40% down, and often a US guarantor — a fallback, not a base case. FLAG: any deal that 'only pencils with SBA-style leverage' should be treated as out of reach; prefer deals that work all-cash or with a seller note secured by the equipment/real estate.
result.hooman_fit: Strong fit for the diligence and optimization side; neutral on the physical ops. Hooman's biggest edge in this category is DILIGENCE ALPHA: the #1 way to avoid overpaying (or buying a lemon) is verifying true cash volume, and for laundromats/car washes that is a data task — regressing water/sewer/electric utility bills against reported revenue to detect inflated SDE, which he can do far better than 99% of buyers. For vending it's per-machine sell-through and route-optimization analytics (dynamic restocking, location scoring) — directly in his wheelhouse. His EE background + mech-eng friends help with equipment assessment (laundry machine age, car-wash pumps/reclaim, gate/keypad systems). Where his AI/data edge is largely IRRELEVANT: the day-to-day is collections, maintenance calls, attendant/driver management, and lease/landlord relations — these are people/ops skills, not technical. Value-creation upside he could actually build: card/app payment + remote monitoring retrofit on an older cash laundromat (raises price, adds data, reduces skim), dynamic pricing on storage/wash, and analytics-driven vending route optimization. Net: he can absolutely run and improve these (especially if he goes full-time), and his analytical edge is a real acquisition advantage, but the moat/return comes from the asset + a good buy price, not from software he writes.

## Executive summary

I ran a head-to-head across all seven categories on cash yield × durability × Hooman-fit × financing-feasibility × downside. SaaS was made to earn its place, not win by default. The result is a barbell, not a single winner.

**#1 if buying one thing: a verified laundromat, all-cash (~$285–500K).** It is the only category that is simultaneously cash-fit for a non-SBA Canadian buyer, high-yield (real 3x-SDE deals throw ~15–25% pre-tax), semi-absentee (5–15 hr/wk, day job optional), AI-/recession-safe, AND directly diligenceable with his exact edge (regressing water/sewer/electric bills against reported revenue to catch inflated cash flow). Lead target: Fords NJ, $285K / $95K SDE / ~3x / ~33% yield, all-cash with a big reserve.

**#2 boring vertical B2B SaaS at ~3x (EH&S/SDS $325K/$110K, or 17-yr email provider $345K/$116K).** The only category where his AI/infra/code skills are true value creation, not a marginal ops tweak — and the best cash yield (~33%). Remote, no E-2 visa. This validates the main-research SaaS conclusion even after widening the aperture.

**#3 recurring-route local service (Camden NJ pest control, $500K/$180K, 1000+ contracts).** Cheap 2.1–2.8x, 30–45% yields, AI-safe; edge is a margin lever, not the moat. **#4 Buncombe NC signage/CNC/plastics fab ($370K/$155K/2.39x)** — cheapest fair-value operating business, overlaps CutLog, but a full-time operator job.

**Financing reality:** No SBA (Canadian, no green card). With the same $500K a US buyer reaches a $1–2M business (10% down); Hooman reaches ~$500K all-cash — roughly 3–4x smaller SDE. His only leverage is a seller note (no citizenship test); Canadian BDC/CSBFP only helps for a Canada-domiciled target. Hands-on US operation likely needs an E-2 visa (#1 diligence item), which is why remote SaaS / semi-absentee assets are cleaner for him. Franchises, self-storage, and car-wash-with-RE are the deals most distorted by no-SBA — demoted.

**Bottom line:** Going wider + full-time DOES beat the part-time plan on absolute income — a real path to $10–18K/mo. But it crowns a barbell: boring vertical SaaS (max edge + yield, remote) OR a verified laundromat (max durability + lowest hours + best all-cash fit). Traps to avoid: Amazon FBA single-brand, SEO/YouTube content (melting), franchises, self-storage. Next steps: verify E-2/residency, run a parallel ON/BC search to unlock BDC leverage, and open diligence on the EH&S SaaS and the Fords NJ laundromat as the two leads.
